directions.description: 神经活动如何表示变量、结构与信息。

群体活动如何关联行为、认知变量和脑区组织。
如何观察、扰动并识别神经系统中的关系。

papers.title: On the Distribution of Firing Rates in Networks of Cortical Neurons

claims.statement: In the analysed fluctuation-driven network models, an expansive single-neuron input-output nonlinearity can transform approximately symmetric input distributions into long-tailed firing-rate distributions.

evidence.description: Analytical and numerical analyses of leaky integrate-and-fire and conductance-based network models.

conclusion.positive: In the analysed fluctuation-driven network models, an expansive single-neuron input-output nonlinearity can transform approximately symmetric input distributions into long-tailed firing-rate distributions.
conclusion.boundary: Randomly connected cortical network models in the parameter regimes analysed in the paper.
conclusion.negative: This does not establish that the same mechanism uniquely explains every empirical cortical firing-rate distribution.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

papers.title: Voltage- and Branch-Specific Climbing Fiber Responses in Purkinje Cells

claims.statement: In the analysed Purkinje-cell models, climbing-fibre responses and their energetic cost depend on dendritic voltage and branch identity.

evidence.description: Compartmental modelling of climbing-fibre input, potassium-current availability, calcium influx and energy consumption.

conclusion.positive: In the analysed Purkinje-cell models, climbing-fibre responses and their energetic cost depend on dendritic voltage and branch identity.
conclusion.boundary: Purkinje-cell dendritic responses under the model and stimulation conditions studied.
conclusion.negative: Somatic complex-spike duration alone is not treated as a complete readout of dendritic climbing-fibre bursting.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

claims.statement: Somatic complex-spike duration does not reliably report the number of climbing-fibre spikes represented in Purkinje-cell dendrites.

evidence.description: Compartmental simulations comparing somatic complex spikes with branch-specific dendritic responses.

conclusion.positive: Dendritic climbing-fibre processing is branch-specific and cannot be reduced to one somatic duration measure.
conclusion.boundary: Established in the detailed Purkinje-cell model and stimulation protocols analysed.
conclusion.negative: A simple monotonic mapping from somatic complex-spike duration to dendritic climbing-fibre bursting was not supported.
conclusion.unresolved: The extent to which the same dissociation holds across in-vivo states remains open.

papers.title: Targeted Activation of Hippocampal Place Cells Drives Memory-Guided Spatial Behavior

claims.statement: Targeted activation of small hippocampal place-cell ensembles biased mice toward the spatial behaviour associated with those cells.

evidence.description: All-optical two-photon imaging and targeted optogenetic stimulation during virtual-reality navigation.

conclusion.positive: Targeted activation of small hippocampal place-cell ensembles biased mice toward the spatial behaviour associated with those cells.
conclusion.boundary: The place-cell ensembles, behavioural task and mouse preparation tested in the study.
conclusion.negative: The result does not imply that place cells alone are sufficient for all forms of spatial memory.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

claims.statement: Targeted place-cell stimulation can disrupt the endogenous place code and trigger remapping in the tested environment.

evidence.description: Simultaneous two-photon calcium imaging and targeted stimulation of identified place-cell ensembles.

conclusion.positive: Artificial activation altered both behaviour and the ongoing hippocampal representation.
conclusion.boundary: Observed for selected ensembles in the virtual-reality task.
conclusion.negative: The stimulated code did not simply add to an otherwise unchanged endogenous map.
conclusion.unresolved: How long the induced remapping persists outside the tested sessions is unresolved.

papers.title: The Neuronal Perturbome in Mouse Visual Cortex

claims.statement: Single-cell perturbations in mouse visual cortex produce heterogeneous local influence patterns that cannot be inferred from activity correlations alone.

evidence.description: Targeted neuronal perturbation combined with population recording in visual cortex.

conclusion.positive: Single-cell perturbations in mouse visual cortex produce heterogeneous local influence patterns that cannot be inferred from activity correlations alone.
conclusion.boundary: Local cortical effects measured in the experimental preparation and visual conditions used by the study.
conclusion.negative: The measured perturbation map is not a complete anatomical connectome or a universal causal circuit model.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

papers.title: Metabolically Regulated Spiking Could Serve Neuronal Energy Homeostasis and Protect from Reactive Oxygen Species

claims.statement: The proposed models show that self-initiated spiking can act as an energy-release mechanism that stabilizes mitochondrial metabolic variables and limits reactive oxygen species under low demand.

evidence.description: Models coupling ATP, ADP and reactive oxygen species to firing, including a ROS-modulated ion-channel model and cortical avalanche simulations.

conclusion.positive: The proposed models show that self-initiated spiking can act as an energy-release mechanism that stabilizes mitochondrial metabolic variables and limits reactive oxygen species under low demand.
conclusion.boundary: A computational existence result under the metabolic assumptions and parameter regimes analysed.
conclusion.negative: The paper does not demonstrate in vivo that metabolic homeostasis is the unique cause of spontaneous neuronal activity.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

claims.statement: Metabolic feedback can sustain avalanche-like network dynamics indefinitely in the cortical models tested.

evidence.description: Network simulations coupling activity-dependent energetic variables to neuronal excitability.

conclusion.positive: The feedback model generated sustained avalanche dynamics without requiring externally imposed critical tuning.
conclusion.boundary: A computational existence result under the selected metabolic dynamics and network parameters.
conclusion.negative: The simulations do not establish that metabolic feedback is necessary for empirical neuronal avalanches.
conclusion.unresolved: Direct experimental discrimination from competing homeostatic mechanisms remains open.

papers.title: A Drosophila Computational Brain Model Reveals Sensorimotor Processing

claims.statement: A whole-brain leaky integrate-and-fire model built from Drosophila connectivity and neurotransmitter identity generated experimentally testable predictions for feeding and grooming circuits.

evidence.description: Connectome-constrained simulation followed by optogenetic and behavioural validation of selected predictions.

conclusion.positive: A whole-brain leaky integrate-and-fire model built from Drosophila connectivity and neurotransmitter identity generated experimentally testable predictions for feeding and grooming circuits.
conclusion.boundary: Adult Drosophila sensorimotor circuits and the model assumptions tested in the paper.
conclusion.negative: Connectivity and transmitter identity are not claimed to explain every neural computation or behavioural context.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

claims.statement: Connectome-constrained activation of feeding-region neurons predicted neurons capable of eliciting motor-neuron firing and feeding behaviour.

evidence.description: Whole-brain simulation followed by targeted optogenetic and behavioural tests.

conclusion.positive: Selected model predictions were validated by perturbing the predicted neurons.
conclusion.boundary: Validated for specific adult-fly feeding circuits and perturbations.
conclusion.negative: Not every prediction of the whole-brain model was experimentally tested.
conclusion.unresolved: Predictive accuracy across untested states and neuromodulatory conditions remains unknown.

claims.statement: The same connectome-constrained model predicted a compact antennal-grooming circuit from mechanosensory input.

evidence.description: Computational activation of mechanosensory subtypes compared with known and measured grooming-circuit responses.

conclusion.positive: The model recovered a small set of neurons associated with antennal grooming responses.
conclusion.boundary: Specific to the mechanosensory pathways and connectome used.
conclusion.negative: The result does not establish complete behavioural prediction from connectivity alone.
conclusion.unresolved: Generalization to other sensorimotor transformations requires further tests.

papers.title: Emergence and Effective Information in Data-Driven Dynamical Systems

claims.statement: Maximizing effective information can learn coarse-grained latent dynamics with stronger estimated causal effects and improved out-of-environment generalization in the tested systems.

evidence.description: Machine-learning framework evaluated on simulated systems, real data and an fMRI coarse-graining example.

conclusion.positive: Maximizing effective information can learn coarse-grained latent dynamics with stronger estimated causal effects and improved out-of-environment generalization in the tested systems.
conclusion.boundary: The causal-emergence objective, models and datasets analysed by the study.
conclusion.negative: A learned macro-state is not automatically a uniquely correct ontology of the underlying system.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

papers.title: High Capacity and Dynamic Accessibility in Associative Memory Networks with Context-Dependent Neuronal and Synaptic Gating

claims.statement: In context-modular associative-memory networks, neuronal or synaptic gating can reduce cross-context interference and trade memory accessibility against storage capacity.

evidence.description: Analytical and numerical study of random gating and context-specific synaptic refinement.

conclusion.positive: In context-modular associative-memory networks, neuronal or synaptic gating can reduce cross-context interference and trade memory accessibility against storage capacity.
conclusion.boundary: The associative-memory model classes and gating protocols introduced in the paper.
conclusion.negative: The framework is not direct evidence that biological memory uses the same gating implementation.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

claims.statement: Context-specific synaptic refinement can increase associative-memory capacity beyond random contextual gating in the analysed networks.

evidence.description: Analytical capacity calculations and numerical comparisons of random gating with synaptic refinement.

conclusion.positive: Removing context-destabilizing synapses improved capacity and control of memory stability.
conclusion.boundary: Derived for the context-modular associative-memory models studied.
conclusion.negative: Random gating was not uniformly optimal across the analysed regimes.
conclusion.unresolved: A biologically local process that implements the refinement rule remains to be established.

papers.title: A General Framework for Interpretable Neural Learning Based on Local Information-Theoretic Goal Functions

claims.statement: Parameterized local goals derived from partial information decomposition can train infomorphic networks on supervised, unsupervised and memory tasks while retaining an interpretable local objective.

evidence.description: Derivation of a local learning rule and computational demonstrations across several learning paradigms.

conclusion.positive: Parameterized local goals derived from partial information decomposition can train infomorphic networks on supervised, unsupervised and memory tasks while retaining an interpretable local objective.
conclusion.boundary: The neuron model, PID parameterization, architectures and tasks evaluated in the paper.
conclusion.negative: Task performance does not by itself establish that the learning rule is biologically implemented.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

papers.title: Linking Functional Activity and Connectivity of Neuronal Circuits via Fast Cross-Layer All-Optical Physiology

claims.statement: The CLAOP system can combine fast cross-layer two-photon recording with targeted optogenetic manipulation to map functional activity-connectivity relations across cortical layers.

evidence.description: Instrument validation and all-optical measurements in visual, somatosensory and hippocampal circuits.

conclusion.positive: The CLAOP system can combine fast cross-layer two-photon recording with targeted optogenetic manipulation to map functional activity-connectivity relations across cortical layers.
conclusion.boundary: The optical preparation, spatial-temporal resolution and circuit examples tested.
conclusion.negative: Functional influence measured by the system is not identical to a complete anatomical connectivity map.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

papers.title: A Brain-Wide Map of Neural Activity during Complex Behaviour

claims.statement: Across a standardized decision task, sensory, choice, movement and prior-related signals were distributed across many brain regions with distinct spatial and temporal profiles.

evidence.description: 621,733 neurons recorded with 699 Neuropixels probes across 139 mice and 12 laboratories.

conclusion.positive: Across a standardized decision task, sensory, choice, movement and prior-related signals were distributed across many brain regions with distinct spatial and temporal profiles.
conclusion.boundary: The standardized mouse decision-making task, recorded areas and analyses reported by the International Brain Laboratory.
conclusion.negative: Widespread encoding does not establish that every recorded region is causally necessary for each variable.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

claims.statement: Visual-stimulus representations were initially concentrated in classical visual areas and later accompanied by ramp-like activity in distributed midbrain and hindbrain regions.

evidence.description: Standardized Neuropixels recordings across 279 brain areas during the same decision task.

conclusion.positive: Different task variables showed distinct temporal and anatomical distributions across the brain.
conclusion.boundary: Descriptive encoding analyses in the standardized task and recorded regions.
conclusion.negative: Distributed encoding alone does not identify causal necessity.
conclusion.unresolved: Which distributed signals causally drive choice remains unresolved by these recordings.

papers.title: Neuromorphic Computing Paradigms Enhance Robustness through Spiking Neural Networks

claims.statement: In the evaluated CIFAR-10 adversarial setting, temporal encoding, early-exit decoding and specialized training improved spiking-network robustness relative to the matched artificial-network baselines.

evidence.description: Adversarial robustness experiments and ablations on temporal processing and encoding strategies.

conclusion.positive: In the evaluated CIFAR-10 adversarial setting, temporal encoding, early-exit decoding and specialized training improved spiking-network robustness relative to the matched artificial-network baselines.
conclusion.boundary: The datasets, attacks, architectures, training methods and energy estimates used in the study.
conclusion.negative: The reported advantage is not a universal robustness guarantee for all spiking networks or attacks.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

claims.statement: Prioritizing task-relevant spikes early and terminating decoding before later perturbations improved adversarial robustness in the tested spiking networks.

evidence.description: Controlled encoding and early-exit ablations under adversarial perturbations on CIFAR-10.

conclusion.positive: Temporal placement of information contributed independently to robustness.
conclusion.boundary: Evaluated for the attacks, encoders, architectures and stopping rules reported.
conclusion.negative: Spiking alone was not sufficient; specialized encoding and training choices mattered.
conclusion.unresolved: Robustness under unseen physical perturbations and broader datasets remains open.

papers.title: Deconstructing Dynamics of Symmetry Breaking

claims.statement: Analytical solutions of order-parameter dynamics in the studied Landau-Ginzburg settings explain why the temporal freeze-out construction reproduces Kibble-Zurek scaling.

evidence.description: Analytical treatment of temporal and spatial order-parameter evolution with proposed experimentally accessible observables.

conclusion.positive: Analytical solutions of order-parameter dynamics in the studied Landau-Ginzburg settings explain why the temporal freeze-out construction reproduces Kibble-Zurek scaling.
conclusion.boundary: The phase-transition models and approximations analysed in the paper.
conclusion.negative: The derivation does not make every real symmetry-breaking system equivalent to the analysed models.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

papers.title: Artificial Neural Manifolds

claims.statement: A Mott-memristor architecture can construct a low-dimensional artificial neural manifold for small-sample prediction, with a memory factor improving robustness in the tested tasks.

evidence.description: Device circuits, delay-embedding formulation and demonstrations on incomplete-image perception and seizure prediction.

conclusion.positive: A Mott-memristor architecture can construct a low-dimensional artificial neural manifold for small-sample prediction, with a memory factor improving robustness in the tested tasks.
conclusion.boundary: The hardware architecture, spatiotemporal information equation and benchmark tasks reported.
conclusion.negative: Similarity to biological tuning curves does not establish biological equivalence.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

claims.statement: Adding a memory factor to the spatiotemporal-information equation improved prediction accuracy and robustness in the evaluated manifold tasks.

evidence.description: Memristor-circuit demonstrations and prediction tests with and without the memory factor.

conclusion.positive: History information improved incomplete-image perception and seizure-prediction performance in the reported tests.
conclusion.boundary: The implemented Mott-memristor architecture and selected datasets.
conclusion.negative: A static manifold equation without the memory factor was less robust in the reported comparisons.
conclusion.unresolved: Scalability and device-to-device variability at larger hardware scales remain open.

papers.title: Human Cortical Networks Trade Communication Efficiency for Computational Reliability

claims.statement: In the study's generative and reservoir-computing analyses, human cortical topology sacrifices wiring and communication efficiency for greater robustness of computation to targeted disruption.

evidence.description: Game-theoretic network growth, reservoir-computing comparison and virtual lesion analyses.

conclusion.positive: In the study's generative and reservoir-computing analyses, human cortical topology sacrifices wiring and communication efficiency for greater robustness of computation to targeted disruption.
conclusion.boundary: Human structural-network data and the propagation, optimization and lesion models used.
conclusion.negative: The result does not imply that communication efficiency is irrelevant or that the model uniquely explains cortical topology.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

claims.statement: Networks optimized for communication efficiency concentrated traffic through a spatially clustered hub oligarchy and were more fragile to targeted lesions than human cortical networks.

evidence.description: Generative network comparison and virtual targeted-lesion experiments.

conclusion.positive: Distributed rich-club organization improved reliability at a cost in wiring and communication efficiency.
conclusion.boundary: Based on the network communication, reservoir and lesion models used.
conclusion.negative: Maximum communication efficiency did not maximize computational reliability.
conclusion.unresolved: Whether the same trade-off governs developmental wiring mechanisms remains open.

papers.title: A Language Network in the Individualized Functional Connectomes of 1199 Human Brains Doing Arbitrary Tasks

claims.statement: Individualized functional connectomes from arbitrary-task fMRI recovered a predominantly left-lateralized frontotemporal network that was stable within people and selective for language.

evidence.description: 1,957 fMRI sessions from 1,199 people analysed with individualized functional connectomics.

conclusion.positive: Individualized functional connectomes from arbitrary-task fMRI recovered a predominantly left-lateralized frontotemporal network that was stable within people and selective for language.
conclusion.boundary: The datasets, preprocessing, parcellations and language-localization tests reported.
conclusion.negative: Functional-connectivity recovery does not uniquely specify the causal computations of language.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

claims.statement: Individualized functional-connectome language networks were more stable within individuals than between individuals across the analysed sessions.

evidence.description: Within- and between-person comparison across 1,957 fMRI sessions from 1,199 brains.

conclusion.positive: The recovered network preserved person-specific topography despite heterogeneous task data.
conclusion.boundary: Functional-connectivity estimates and datasets included in the study.
conclusion.negative: A single group-average topography did not capture all individual variation.
conclusion.unresolved: The developmental origins and causal consequences of the individual differences remain unresolved.

papers.title: Preconfigured Neuronal Firing Sequences in Human Brain Organoids

claims.statement: Structured spontaneous firing sequences appeared in human and mouse brain organoids and neonatal mouse cortical slices, but not in dissociated primary cortical cultures.

evidence.description: Cross-preparation recordings and sequence analyses in organoids, ex vivo cortex and dissociated cultures.

conclusion.positive: Structured spontaneous firing sequences appeared in human and mouse brain organoids and neonatal mouse cortical slices, but not in dissociated primary cortical cultures.
conclusion.boundary: The developmental stages, preparations and sequence metrics tested.
conclusion.negative: The observations do not show that all mature sequence structure is independent of experience.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

claims.statement: Structured spontaneous sequences were absent from the dissociated primary cortical cultures used as a comparison.

evidence.description: Matched sequence analyses across organoids, neonatal cortical slices and dissociated cultures.

conclusion.positive: Sequence structure depended on preparation-level circuit organization rather than neuronal activity alone.
conclusion.boundary: Limited to the preparations, ages and detection methods tested.
conclusion.negative: Dissociated cultures did not reproduce the structured sequences observed in organoids and slices.
conclusion.unresolved: Which architectural features are necessary for sequence formation remains unresolved.

papers.title: Simple Input-Output Dependencies Explain Neuronal Activity

claims.statement: Across the neuronal datasets studied, models containing direct input-output dependencies without explicit input interactions explained most measured activity variability and predicted higher-order dependencies.

evidence.description: Quantitative model comparison across multiple brain regions and species, with inferred connectivity analyses.

conclusion.positive: Across the neuronal datasets studied, models containing direct input-output dependencies without explicit input interactions explained most measured activity variability and predicted higher-order dependencies.
conclusion.boundary: The binary activity representations, datasets and dependency models analysed.
conclusion.negative: Good predictive performance does not establish that biophysical input interactions are absent.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

claims.statement: Models containing only direct input-output dependencies predicted higher-order activity dependencies without explicitly fitting input interactions.

evidence.description: Out-of-sample comparison of minimal dependency models with measured multi-neuron activity statistics.

conclusion.positive: Complex population dependencies can emerge from combinations of simple direct dependencies in the tested datasets.
conclusion.boundary: Binary representations and neuronal datasets analysed in the paper.
conclusion.negative: Explicit interaction terms were not required to explain most measured variability in these analyses.
conclusion.unresolved: Biophysical interactions may still matter outside the measured statistics and timescales.

papers.title: Predictability of Complex Networks

claims.statement: Mapping link prediction to a spin-glass model yields a predictability index and decomposes global link predictability into local contributions in the analysed network ensembles.

evidence.description: Cavity-method derivations, exact results for canonical models and analyses of real networks.

conclusion.positive: Mapping link prediction to a spin-glass model yields a predictability index and decomposes global link predictability into local contributions in the analysed network ensembles.
conclusion.boundary: The link-prediction formulation, random division protocol and network models considered.
conclusion.negative: The predictability index is not a guarantee that every practical algorithm reaches the bound.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

papers.title: Population Geometry Reveals Shared Latent Structure

claims.statement: The study links specific population-geometry statistics to task-efficient representation of shared latent structure across the tested settings.

evidence.description: Population-geometry analyses and computational comparisons reported in the paper.

conclusion.positive: The study links specific population-geometry statistics to task-efficient representation of shared latent structure across the tested settings.
conclusion.boundary: The neural datasets, latent variables and target computations evaluated.
conclusion.negative: Geometric similarity does not by itself establish a unique neural mechanism.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

papers.title: Emotional-State Geometry in the Basolateral Amygdala

claims.statement: Basolateral-amygdala population activity in the tested threat paradigm contained a geometry that supported specialized readout of emotional state across behavioural conditions.

evidence.description: Population recordings, behavioural measurements, decoding and perturbation analyses in mice.

conclusion.positive: Basolateral-amygdala population activity in the tested threat paradigm contained a geometry that supported specialized readout of emotional state across behavioural conditions.
conclusion.boundary: The virtual-burrow assay, aversive conditions and recorded basolateral-amygdala populations.
conclusion.negative: The geometry is not asserted to be a complete or universal representation of emotion.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.

papers.title: Machine, Organism and Language: An Epistemology of AI Models

claims.statement: The essay argues that contemporary AI is best understood through the historical recombination of machine, organism and language paradigms, and as an automation of relational structures embedded in social cooperation.

evidence.description: Comparative historical and philosophical analysis drawing on epistemology, political economy and histories of computation.

conclusion.positive: The essay argues that contemporary AI is best understood through the historical recombination of machine, organism and language paradigms, and as an automation of relational structures embedded in social cooperation.
conclusion.boundary: A conceptual argument rather than an empirical or causal neuroscience claim.
conclusion.negative: The essay does not experimentally test a computational mechanism or biological model.
conclusion.unresolved: Not resolved by this source alone.
